title: Write off broken, expired, or missing stock
text: Loss & Damage takes items you cannot sell out of stock and records why. Reports then show what keeps costing you money.
steps: Select a product and enter the lost quantity.
Select a reason and add a note.

title: Add a new loss reason
text: Reasons live in a dropdown so they stay the same every time. You can add one without leaving the editor.
steps: Click Add New and enter the reason.

title: Save a loss record as a draft
text: A draft keeps your rows without changing any stock. The reason is only required when you finally save.
steps: Open its menu and click Edit Loss & Damage.
Finish the record and click Save.

title: Write off a batch that is expiring
text: Expired or soon-to-expire stock is a Loss & Damage record because it can no longer be sold. You can start the record from the batch or expiry details when that shortcut is available.
steps: Check the product, batch, expiry, and quantity.
Select an expiry reason and add a note.

title: Which Stock Record Should I Use?
text: Use Loss & Damage when stock is damaged or missing. Use another stock record when the quantity is simply wrong.
steps: Damaged or missing stock? Use Loss & Damage.
Wrong stock number? Use Stock Adjustment.

title: Cannot write off more than you have
text: A loss cannot be bigger than the quantity on hand. If the shelf is emptier than the system thinks, fix the number first.
steps: Fix wrong stock in Stock Adjustment first.

title: Review what has been written off
text: Every record stays in the list with its reference and reason. Group them by period to see trends.
steps: Search by reference, reason, or period.
Open a row and click View Loss & Damage.
Use Print & Export for a copy.

title: Record several lost products together
text: One Loss & Damage record can include more than one product. Add every item from the same incident so the stock movement and note stay together.
steps: Select each product and enter its lost quantity.
Select a reason and add a note.
Check the rows and click Save.

title: Add useful details to a loss record
text: A short note makes a loss easier to check later. Include what happened, where it happened, and any reference or staff detail your business uses.
steps: Add the incident details in Note.

title: Avoid recording the same loss twice
text: Save one record for each incident. Before saving a new one, search the list for the date, product, reason, or reference so the same missing stock is not deducted twice.
steps: Search by product, reason, reference, or period.
Do not record the same incident twice.
For a new incident, click New Loss & Damage and save once.

title: Understand what happens after saving a loss
text: A saved loss reduces the product quantity immediately and remains in the Loss & Damage list. Use the reference, reason, and period to trace it in stock history and reports.
steps: Check the product and Loss/Damage Qty.
Open Loss & Damage to see the saved record.
Use Action > View Loss & Damage to check its details.

title: Understand the Loss & Damage detail panel
text: The Loss & Damage detail panel lists each selected product and the values needed to calculate the write-off. Stock shows the quantity on hand, Loss/Damage Qty is the quantity being recorded, and Cost shows the cost of the affected items.
steps: Open a new Loss & Damage record.
Search for and select a product.
Check Cost and confirm the product is correct.

title: Review loss totals before saving
text: The summary at the bottom of the Loss & Damage form shows the Total Qty and Total Cost for all products in the record. Review both totals before posting the loss.
steps: Check the summary at the bottom.

title: Save, draft, or cancel a loss record
text: Save posts the Loss & Damage record and updates inventory. Save as Draft keeps the work for later without posting it, while Cancel discards the record without changing stock.
steps: Select a reason and check the quantities.
Click Save to post the loss.
Click Save as Draft to finish later.

title: Read the Loss & Damage dashboard
text: The Loss & Damage dashboard lists recorded transactions and their reference number, transaction date, status, reason, total quantity, total cost, overall cost, and note.
steps: Find the record by Reference Number.
Check its date and Posted or Draft status.
Review the reason, quantities, costs, and note.
Open the Action menu for details.

title: View a Loss & Damage transaction
text: View Loss & Damage shows the transaction header and each affected product. It includes the reference, date, reason, notes, product name, barcode, expiration, actual quantity before the loss, Loss/Damage Qty, unit cost, and total cost.
steps: Check the reference, date, reason, and notes.
Check each product's barcode, expiry, quantities, and costs.
